title: Preference Leakage: A Contamination Problem in LLM-as-a-judge

live_model.resolved: gpt-4o-2024-11-20 (dated snapshot, not on the still-callable list)
live_model.evidence: "We choose three powerful LLMs as data generator/judge models. They are GPT-4o-2024-11-20 ... Gemini-1.5-flash ... and LLaMA-3.3-70B-Instruct-turbo" (Sec. 4.1 Experiment Setup)

prompt.location: Sec. 4.1 (pairwise judging on Arena-Hard/AlpacaEval 2.0 templates), Appendix
prompt.note: Standard Arena-Hard / AlpacaEval 2.0 pairwise-judge prompting; exact wording not quoted in the main text.

claim.metric: Preference Leakage Score (PLS, %), GPT-4o judge/data-generator vs. Gemini-1.5 pair, Mistral student, AlpacaEval 2.0

data.source: Arena-Hard (500 questions), AlpacaEval 2.0 (805 questions), UltraFeedback (30,000 sampled prompts) -- all public

notes: ICLR 2026. The judge/data-generator model is pinned to gpt-4o-2024-11-20, a dated snapshot that is not among the still-callable identifiers (only gpt-4o-2024-05-13 is tracked), so the paper's central claim cannot be re-run on a live model as specified. Full pipeline also requires supervised fine-tuning of student models on 30k generated responses before judging, adding further cost beyond simple prompting.
